outcome: Wired GS-1..GS-5 and GS-7 into the existing lib/human-guard-override.mjs family in plugins/pipeline-core/hooks/guard-gate-strength.mjs, in the same consume-first-then-offer-mode-appropriate-route shape guard-testpath.mjs already uses: read tool_name/tool_input in the CLI entrypoint, attempt consumeHumanGuardOverride() for any matched rule other than LIVE_PLUGIN_RULE, exit 0 with a [pipeline-human-override] audit line on consume, and otherwise recordHumanGuardDenial() plus a chat- or signature-shaped next-step block appended to the unchanged refusal. GS-6 is excluded and keeps its separate ADR-0058 Guard Maintenance Window. The file header's old claim that there is deliberately no in-session override was rewritten for GS-1..5/7 and kept verbatim for GS-6, and now records why admitting a chat-armed capability is not an escalation: HGO-SIGNATURE-MODE-REQUIRED refuses to arm any chat-mode capability for any path unless the repository's committed mode is already chat, which is itself a GS-protected edit.
designCorrection: This dispatch was redirected mid-run. Its original briefing specified an unconditional chat-mode ban for GATE_STRENGTH_PATHS, i.e. signature-only regardless of configuration. The PO rejected that before anything was committed, citing a standing decision already recorded in ADR-0056 Decision 4 that the Elephant should not have re-litigated per guard. The escalation worry motivating the rejected design was then verified unreachable, the dispatch was redirected to the corrected design via SendMessage, and the standing principle was written into ADR-0059 after Decision 3 so it does not need rediscovering again.
testCoverage: NONE, and disclosed rather than worked around. The guard's own suite is plugins/pipeline-core/hooks/guard-gate-strength.test.mjs, which TP-6 protects, so the dispatch could not extend it; it began writing a throwaway scratchpad harness instead and was cut off mid-sentence by its own budget before producing or reporting any result from it. The committed change therefore carries review evidence only, never execution evidence. node --check passes and the imports resolve (verified by the Elephant, not by the dispatch). A maintenance window covering TP-2/TP-6/TP-7 is the unblocking step; the tests follow it.
orchestratorCompletion: The dispatch never reported.
